text:
Sam: Heads-up — seeing a p99 latency spike on g5x pools starting ~03:10 UTC. Throughput dropped and we've got an uptick in kernel fallbacks to cudnn/cuBLAS for short-seq traffic. Investigating.
InfraBot: Alert triggered: latency.p99 > 900ms (service: inference-g5x, window: 5m).
Jess: Impact - how many requests and which routes?
Sam: Roughly 8% of requests for seq<=32 experienced fallbacks, p99 jumped from ~600ms -> ~1.2s for those routes. Affected model: rwd/encoder-64 (short chat workloads).
Mike E.: Can you paste selector/runtime logs + any nsys snippets?
Sam: Selector excerpt: ```[2026-03-18T03:09:58Z] model=rwd/encoder-64 seq=32 batch=12 chosen_kernel=triton_flashkernel_v2 alloc_status=ok launch_status=fallback reason="workspace_alloc_fail" driver_version=535.86``` Runtime note: fallback_count++ and kernel_run=cudnn_gemm.
Anya: We rolled driver 535.86 to canary yesterday evening. Might correlate.
Mike E.: That "workspace_alloc_fail" + driver bump smells like allocator interaction under KV prefetch pressure. Any KV cache growth on those requests?
Sam: Yes — runtime profiling shows a transient KV prefetch bump for a subset of tenants (prefix caching growth ~18-22% extra memory during warmup). When batches align, workspace footprint + KV pages exceed allocable region and kernel launch falls back.
Sam: nsys snippet (summarized): ```flash_attn_cuda  runtime  18.7ms  achieved=12TFLOPS  status=failed_launch -> fallback; cudnn_gemm runtime  54.2ms  achieved=3TFLOPS```
Jess: Oof. So fallback is both slower and more memory-hungry in practice for these shapes.
Kevin R.: Can we repro on a repro host? If it's driver-level, local repro with driver 535.86 vs 534.x would be instructive.
Mike E.: I ran a local repro on g5x canary: ``./perf_test --model rwd/encoder-64 --seq 32 --batch 12 --kv-prefetch=on`` — saw the same failure pattern. Kernel-selector heuristic chose triton_flashkernel_v2, but cuda returned workspace error and runtime fell back.
Sam: Immediate mitigations proposed: 1) roll back driver 535.86 on canary g5x (quick), 2) temporarily change kernel-selector tiebreaker to prefer stable cuDNN path for batches>10 (safety), 3) add KV prefetch cap per-request to avoid transient workspace spikes.
Anya: I'll draft a KV-prefetch limiter PR (small guard: cap additional prefetch pages to X% of base).
Kevin R.: I'll coordinate driver rollback on canary nodes now. @Jess will monitor. :eyes:
Mike E.: I'll prepare a selector hotfix to add a workspace-estimate check before choosing triton_flashkernel_v2. That should prevent a lot of these falls.
Jess: Noted. I'm updating the incident slack channel and paging oncall. Pager rule: kernel-fallback-rate >5% for 10m.
InfraBot: Deploy started: rollback/driver/535.86 -> 534.21 (canary: 4 hosts).
Sam: After driver rollback to 534.21 on the 4 canary hosts, preliminary metrics: fallback rate dropped from 8% -> 1.4%, p99 for affected routes fell from ~1.2s -> ~640ms. Still above baseline but much better.
Mike E.: Will push selector guard and a metric for fallback_rate/model in the next 30m.
Anya: KV limiter PR up next; will include a small dry-run flag so we can observe effect before enabling.
Sam: Postmortem action items: - track kernel fallback rate per model/host - add workspace_estimate guard in selector - KV prefetch cap + telemetry - add driver-version canary gating to avoid broad rollout without perf smoke tests.
Jess: Thanks everyone. I'll keep monitoring for the next 2 hours and reopen if we see regression. :thumbsup:
Kevin R.: Filing a short blameless note in incidents/ after we confirm rollback stability.
Sam: Closing thread for now — will follow up with PR links and perf graphs.
